mainTopic: Missing אחריות in a כתובה; when a raped or captive wife stays permitted to her husband; redeeming a כהן's wife
overview: The גמרא finishes a משנה showing that רבי מאיר treats a missing אחריות clause as truly missing. It then asks how our משנה can follow one opinion, and answers in two ways: the whole משנה is רבי יהודה, or the whole משנה is רבי מאיר and "obligated" means only from free property. Next, אבוה דשמואל rules that a raped wife of an ישראל is forbidden, because she may have ended up willing. The גמרא defends him: captives are a special leniency, and a forced woman is permitted when witnesses saw her scream the whole time. רבא disagrees and holds that what starts as אונס stays אונס. Three teachings on "והיא לא נתפשה" each find a different exception. רב יהודה rules that kidnapped women stay permitted, because helping their captors comes from fear. Two ברייתות about women taken by kings and by bandits are reconciled through אחשורוש, בן נצר and ordinary bandits. Finally, אביי rules that a כהן גדול must redeem a widow he married.

steps.title: The end of the משנה about found loan documents
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says a document with an אחריות clause may not be returned, but one without it may be returned, since the court won't collect from sold property with it. The חכמים say neither may be returned.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the documents include a property guarantee, he should not return them, because the court collects from sold property with them. If they do not include a property guarantee, he should return them, because the court does not collect from sold property with them. These are the words of רבי מאיר. The חכמים say: in both cases he should not return them, because the court collects with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote from a משנה about someone who finds loan documents. It is setting up a source that it will use for a challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that the loan was already paid, and the borrower and lender might team up to take land the borrower sold to buyers. רבי מאיר says that worry only exists if the document has an אחריות clause, so he treats a missing clause as truly missing. The חכמים say the court collects either way, because they treat a missing clause as a scribe's mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: Property guarantee: a clause putting a lien on the debtor's land, even land he later sells
He should not return it (the finder may not give the document back)
Collect payment (here, from buyers of the borrower's property)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר is the one who says to return documents WITHOUT אחריות. That is because he holds such a document cannot be used against buyers, so a missing clause really means no lien.

phrases.english: If they include a property guarantee —
phrases.notes: "They" are loan documents that someone found. The quote from the משנה started before this line.

phrases.english: he should not return them,
because the court collects with them.
phrases.notes: He means collecting from people who bought the borrower's land.

phrases.english: If they do not include a property guarantee —

phrases.aramaic: יַחֲזִיר, שֶׁאֵין בֵּית דִּין נִפְרָעִין מֵהֶן,
phrases.english: he should return them, because the court does not collect with them,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה לֹא יַחֲזִיר,
phrases.english: And the Sages say: in both this case and that case, he should not return them,
because the court collects with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: יֵשׁ בָּהֶן אַחְרָיוּת נְכָסִים לֹא יַחֲזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a משנה quoted from before this section, to show how רבי מאיר views a missing אחריות clause.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: a document without אחריות cannot collect from sold property. חכמים: it can, because the missing clause is treated as a scribe's mistake.

steps.title: Our משנה seems to follow two different opinions
steps.stepSummary: The first clause of our משנה follows רבי מאיר, but the last clause follows רבי יהודה. Can one משנה be split like that?
steps.simpleTranslation: So the first clause is רבי מאיר and the last clause is רבי יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא complains that our משנה in כתובות seems to switch opinions in the middle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause, that a woman collects her כתובה even if none was written, matches רבי מאיר. The last clause says the husband owes אחריות even if he never wrote it, which treats a missing clause as a scribe's mistake. That is the opposite of רבי מאיר's view in the משנה just quoted, and the גמרא assigns it to רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: The first clause is Rabbi Meir
phrases.notes: This goes back to our own משנה in כתובות, not the one about found documents.

phrases.english: and the last clause is Rabbi Yehuda!

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישָׁא רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְסֵיפָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי מאיר's view from step 1 to show that the last clause of our משנה cannot be his.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that our משנה follows one תנא throughout
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר holds a missing אחריות clause really means no lien, yet the last clause of our משנה gives the woman אחריות without it being written.

steps.title: A possible answer: רבי מאיר treats a כתובה differently
steps.stepSummary: Maybe the whole משנה is רבי מאיר, and he treats a כתובה differently from ordinary loan documents.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say the whole משנה is רבי מאיר, and רבי מאיר distinguishes between a כתובה and other documents...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a way to save the משנה: the whole thing is רבי מאיר, and for him a כתובה is different. This answer is only being proposed so the גמרא can test it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By this suggestion, רבי מאיר holds a missing אחריות clause counts as missing only in ordinary loan documents. In a כתובה, the אחריות would apply even if it was not written. That would make both clauses fit רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a suggested answer)
All of it, the whole משנה
It is different for him; he distinguishes

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא כּוּלַּהּ רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא,
phrases.english: And if you will say the whole משנה is Rabbi Meir,
and Rabbi Meir distinguishes
between a כתובה and other documents.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא כּוּלַּהּ רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible defense against the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases (a כתובה compared with loan documents)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is split between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: All of it is רבי מאיר, who would treat a כתובה's missing אחריות as a mistake but not a loan document's.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows no difference between a כתובה and a loan document
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggested difference. A ברייתא lists a loan document without אחריות and a כתובה without אחריות together, as both collecting only from free property.
steps.simpleTranslation: But does he really distinguish? Was it not taught: Five things are collected only from free property, and they are: produce, improvement of produce, one who took on himself to feed his wife's son or daughter, a loan document without a guarantee, and a woman's כתובה without a guarantee.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether רבי מאיר really treats a כתובה differently, and quotes a ברייתא that seems to say no.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא puts a כתובה without אחריות in exactly the same group as a loan document without אחריות. Both can be collected only from property the debtor still owns, not from buyers. So a missing clause in a כתובה is treated as truly missing, just like in a loan document, which seems to defeat the answer in step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: But is it really so? (opens a challenge)
Free property: land the debtor still owns and has not sold

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא treats a כתובה without אחריות exactly like a loan document without אחריות: both collect only from free property. That undercuts the idea that רבי מאיר distinguishes between them.
steps.confusionAlert: Here "גט" does not mean a divorce document. It is just a document, and גט חוב means a loan document.

phrases.english: But does he really distinguish?
But was it not taught: Five things are collected only from free property,
phrases.notes: Free property is land the debtor still owns, so buyers of his land are never touched.

phrases.english: and these are they: produce, and improvement of produce,
and one who takes upon himself to feed
his wife's son or his wife's daughter,
and a loan document that has no property guarantee,
and a woman's כתובה that has no property guarantee.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the distinction proposed in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי מאיר treats a כתובה differently from loan documents
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא groups a כתובה without אחריות with a loan document without אחריות, so both are treated the same and neither collects from sold property.

steps.title: The ברייתא must follow רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: Only רבי מאיר holds that leaving out אחריות is deliberate and not a טעות סופר. So the ברייתא that puts a כתובה together with a loan document must be his. That proves he treats them the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who do we know says that leaving out the property guarantee is not a scribal mistake? רבי מאיר. Yet that same ברייתא includes a woman's כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows who wrote the ברייתא from the last step, so the challenge now has full force.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a document without אחריות collects only from free property. That is רבי מאיר's view, not רבי יהודה's. Since the same ברייתא lists a כתובה too, רבי מאיר clearly does not separate a כתובה from other documents, and the answer from step 3 falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Whom have you heard say this? The גמרא uses it to figure out who wrote an unnamed source.
The property guarantee clause, which lets a creditor collect from property that was sold

phrases.english: Whom have you heard who says
that leaving out the property guarantee is not a scribal error?
Rabbi Meir.
And yet it teaches a woman's marriage contract too.
phrases.notes: "It" is the ברייתא from the last step, which listed a כתובה right next to a loan document.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge from step 4 by showing that the ברייתא belongs to רבי מאיר.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר makes no special rule for a כתובה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that lists a loan document and a כתובה without אחריות together. Only רבי מאיר holds that leaving out אחריות is deliberate.

steps.title: First answer: the whole משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers two possible answers. In the first, the whole משנה is רבי יהודה. When רבי יהודה lets a woman get less than the full כתובה, it is only because she wrote "I have received." Here she wrote no such thing, so she collects the full amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it is רבי מאיר, and if you want, say it is רבי יהודה. If you say רבי יהודה: there, she wrote him "I have received." Here, she did not write him "I have received."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says it has two ways out, and starts with the first one: the whole משנה can be רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause of the משנה looked like רבי מאיר, because she collects the full כתובה even when nothing was written. The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה agrees here. He only lets her get less when she actively gave up part of it by writing "I have received." When she did not write that, the full rule applies, so both clauses fit רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say. It introduces one of two possible answers.
I have received. The woman writes this to give up part of her כתובה.
There / here. It sets up the contrast between two cases.

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא names both answers at the start, but it explains them in reverse order. The רבי יהודה answer comes first, here, and the רבי מאיר answer comes in the next step.

phrases.english: If you want, say it is Rabbi Meir,
and if you want, say it is Rabbi Yehuda.
If you want, say Rabbi Yehuda:
there, she wrote to him "I have received,"
phrases.notes: "There" is the case where רבי יהודה lets her get less than the full כתובה. She gave up part of it in writing.

phrases.english: here, she did not write to him "I have received."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר, וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 2, which step 5 made stronger, by giving the whole משנה to רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Making a distinction between cases. She gives up part of the כתובה only with a written waiver.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first clause, where she collects the full amount without anything written, must be רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה also gives her the full amount unless she wrote "I have received," so the whole משנה fits רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Second answer: the whole משנה follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: In the second answer, the whole משנה is רבי מאיר. The word "obligated" in the last clause only means he must pay from his free property, not from property he sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it is רבי מאיר. What does the "obligated" that it teaches mean? From the free property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other way out. It reads the last clause in a way that fits רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last clause said he is "obligated" even without an אחריות clause, which sounded like רבי יהודה. Now the גמרא limits that word. He is obligated, but only from property he still owns. That is exactly רבי מאיר's view, so both clauses now fit רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Free property: property the debtor still owns that is not tied to anyone else

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers. In the רבי יהודה answer, a woman gets less only if she wrote "I have received." In the רבי מאיר answer, "obligated" means he pays only from his free property.

phrases.english: If you want, say Rabbi Meir:
what is the "obligated" that it teaches?
phrases.notes: This is the last clause of the משנה, where nothing was written about the guarantee and he is still "obligated."

phrases.english: From the free property.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר: מַאי ״חַיָּיב״ דְּקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the second option announced in step 6. It gives the whole משנה to רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading a word in the משנה more narrowly
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "Obligated" means he pays even from sold property, like רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: "Obligated" means he pays only from his free property, which fits רבי מאיר.

steps.title: A married woman who was raped is forbidden to her husband
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, about ransoming a captive wife. אבוה דשמואל rules that the wife of an ישראל who was raped is forbidden to her husband. The worry is that she may have started out forced but ended up willing.
steps.simpleTranslation: "If he did not write for her," etc. שמואל's father said: the wife of an ישראל who was raped is forbidden to her husband. We worry that it may have started by force and ended willingly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic from the next part of the משנה with a ruling from אבוה דשמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a woman who was forced is not forbidden to her husband. אבוה דשמואל worries that she may have agreed partway through, and a married woman who is willing becomes forbidden. So he treats her as forbidden. This sets up the coming discussion about the משנה's promise to take a ransomed wife back.

keyTerms.meaning: We are concerned. The halacha takes a possibility into account.
It began by force and ended willingly

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling seems to clash with the משנה, which says the husband must ransom her and take her back. That sets up the next part of the סוגיא.

phrases.english: "If he did not write for her," etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. Even if he did not write that he would ransom her and take her back, he is still obligated.

phrases.english: Shmuel's father said:
The wife of an Israelite who was raped
is forbidden to her husband.
We are concerned
that perhaps it began by force
and ended willingly.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא כָּתַב לָהּ וְכוּ׳. אָמַר אֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new section that moves on to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A married woman who was raped is forbidden to her husband, because she may have become willing partway through.

steps.title: רב challenges from the captive-wife clause of the כתובה
steps.stepSummary: רב objects to אבוה דשמואל from the כתובה clause promising to redeem a captive wife and take her back. אבוה דשמואל does not answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב challenged אבוה דשמואל: the כתובה says, "If you are taken captive, I will redeem you and take you back as my wife"! He was silent.
steps.whatsHappening: רב attacks the ruling from Step 8 using our own משנה. The husband promises to take back his captive wife, even though she may have been forced while captive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a forced wife were forbidden because she might have become willing, a captive wife should be forbidden too. Yet the כתובה clause assumes she goes back to her husband. אבוה דשמואל gives no reply.

keyTerms.meaning: I will redeem you (pay your ransom)

phrases.english: Rav raised an objection to Shmuel's father:
"If you are taken captive, I will redeem you
and restore you to me as a wife"!
He was silent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of אבוה דשמואל from Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling of אבוה דשמואל that a raped wife of an ישראל is forbidden to her husband.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The כתובה assumes a captive wife returns to her husband, even though she may have been forced. That contradicts the worry that she ended up willing.

steps.title: רב's verse about the silence, and what could have been answered
steps.stepSummary: רב applies a פסוק about princes who held back their words. The גמרא asks what answer אבוה דשמואל actually had.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said about אבוה דשמואל: "The princes held back their words and put a hand over their mouths." What could he have said?
steps.whatsHappening: רב's פסוק describes great people who choose to keep quiet. It hints that אבוה דשמואל had an answer but did not give it, so the גמרא asks what that answer was. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is about princes, people of stature, who hold back speech on purpose. It does not describe someone with nothing to say. That is why the גמרא looks for the answer he could have given.

keyTerms.meaning: What is there for him to say?

phrases.english: Rav recited about Shmuel's father:
"The princes refrained from talking
and laid a hand upon their mouths."
What is there for him to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the silence in Step 9 and asks what defense was available.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What answer אבוה דשמואל could have given to רב's challenge.

steps.title: With a captive woman the חכמים were lenient
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the captive-wife case is a special leniency, so it does not disprove the ruling about a woman who was certainly raped.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a captive woman, they were lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the answer אבוה דשמואל could have given. The case of a captive is special, and the חכמים were lenient there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a captive, we do not even know that she was violated at all. So the חכמים let her return to her husband. That leniency says nothing about a woman we know was raped, where the worry that she ended up willing still applies.

phrases.english: With a captive woman they were lenient.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10 and defends against Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: a special leniency for a captive.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The captive-wife clause shows that any forced wife of an ישראל is permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: A captive is only possibly violated, so the חכמים were lenient. A woman known to be raped can still be forbidden.

steps.title: By his view, when is the Torah's permitted אונס ever possible?
steps.stepSummary: The Torah permits a forced woman to her husband. If we always fear she ended up willing, when would that permission ever apply?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to אבוה דשמואל, how can you find the case of אונס that the Torah permits?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אבוה דשמואל again. If every forced woman might have become willing, the Torah's rule that a forced woman is permitted seems to have no case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah clearly permits a woman who was truly forced. A ruling that forbids every raped wife seems to cancel that permission completely. So the גמרא asks for a case where his view still allows it.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you find it (a case like this)?

phrases.english: And according to Shmuel's father,
rape where the Merciful One permits her,
how can you find it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלַאֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל אוֹנֶס דְּשַׁרְיַהּ רַחֲמָנָא הֵיכִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to the view in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The worry of אבוה דשמואל that a forced woman may have ended up willing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that worry always applies, the Torah's permission for a forced woman would never apply.

steps.title: Witnesses saw her screaming the whole time
steps.stepSummary: The permitted case is when witnesses testify that she screamed from beginning to end.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, when witnesses say she screamed from the beginning to the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of Step 12. When witnesses saw that she kept screaming the whole time, she is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Screaming all the way to the end shows she never became willing. That removes the worry of אבוה דשמואל. So the Torah's permission still has a real case.

phrases.english: For example, where witnesses say
that she screamed from beginning to end.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: By this view, no forced woman could ever be permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: She is permitted when witnesses show she resisted the whole time.

steps.title: רבא disagrees: even if it ends willingly, she is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that אבוה דשמואל argues with רבא. רבא holds that anything that started as אונס stays אונס, even if she ends up willing, because her desire took over.
steps.simpleTranslation: This argues with רבא. רבא said: Whenever it starts by force and ends willingly, she is permitted. This is true even if she says "leave him" and that she would have paid him if he had not started. Why? Her desire overpowered her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבא holds the opposite of אבוה דשמואל. רבא says a woman forced at the start is permitted, even if she became willing at the end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אבוה דשמואל, ending willingly makes her forbidden. For רבא, what started by force counts as force all the way through, because the desire it stirred up overpowered her. So by רבא, the worry from Step 8 does not apply at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The inclination took hold of her (literally, clothed her)

steps.whatToRemember: אבוה דשמואל: a forced woman who may have ended willing is forbidden; she is permitted only if witnesses saw her resist to the end. Captives are a special leniency. רבא: once it started by force, it is all אונס, and she is permitted.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying a fully willing act is permitted. He means the willingness at the end grew out of the force at the start, so the act still counts as forced.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the earlier answers defending אבוה דשמואל rest on a view רבא does not share.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rava.
As Rava said:
Any case that starts as rape
and ends willingly, even
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording, filling in what the sentence needs.

phrases.english: if she says: Leave him,
that if he had not engaged with her,
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets is left out of the corrected wording, since אִלְמָלֵא already means "if not."

phrases.english: she would have hired him,
she is permitted.
What is the reason?
The inclination took hold of her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts the view defended in Steps 11 and 13 with the opposing view of רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anything that starts as אונס and ends willingly still counts as אונס, so she remains permitted to her husband.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the פסוק about סוטה to include a woman whose relationship began forced and ended willing, and says she is permitted. This matches רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא agrees with רבא. The פסוק says 'and she was not taken,' so if she was not forced, she is forbidden. That means if she was forced, she is permitted. But there is another case where she was not forced and is still permitted: any case that began by force and ended willingly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רבא's rule from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The simple reading of the פסוק is that only a forced woman is permitted. The ברייתא adds a case where she is not fully forced and is still permitted: one that started as אונס and ended with רצון. That is exactly רבא's position.
steps.whyThisMatters: This makes רבא's view stronger against אבוה דשמואל, who worried that a woman who ended up willing would be forbidden.

phrases.english: It is taught in agreement with Rava:
"And she was not taken" — she is forbidden.
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:13, about a סוטה. 'Taken' here means taken by force.

phrases.english: This implies that if she was taken, she is permitted.
And you have another case,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נִתְפָּשָׂה — מוּתֶּרֶת,
phrases.english: where even though she was not taken, she is permitted.
And which case is it? It is
any case that begins by force and ends willingly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support from a ברייתא for רבא's rule in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that what begins as אונס stays אונס, even if it ends willingly.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading of 'והיא לא נתפשה' that lists 'started forced, ended willing' as permitted.

steps.title: Another ברייתא: a כהן's wife is forbidden even if forced
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא uses the same פסוק to point to the opposite kind of exception: a כהן's wife, who is forbidden even when she was forced.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: 'And she was not taken,' so she is forbidden. That means if she was taken, she is permitted. But there is another case where she was forced and is still forbidden: the wife of a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא that reads the same פסוק but finds a different special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the exception goes the other way. Normally a forced woman is permitted to her husband, but the wife of a כהן is forbidden to him even after אונס.
steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא is not arguing that אונס is forbidden in general. It is only pointing out one exception: a כהן's wife.

phrases.english: Another [baraita] teaches:
"And she was not taken" — she is forbidden.
This implies that if she was taken, she is permitted.
And you have another case,
where even though she was taken, she is forbidden.
And which case is it? It is the wife of a priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same פסוק and the same pattern as step 15, but finds a different exception.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן's wife who was forced is forbidden to her husband.

steps.title: A third reading: a girl whose marriage can be ended by מיאון
steps.stepSummary: In the name of רבי ישמעאל, the exception is a girl whose marriage was a 'mistaken' one. She can leave through מיאון, so she stays permitted even if she was not forced.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל, quoting רבי ישמעאל: 'And she was not taken,' so she is forbidden. That means if she was taken, she is permitted. But there is another case where she was not forced and is still permitted: a girl whose marriage was a mistaken marriage. Even with her son riding on her shoulders, she can refuse and walk away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third teaching on the same פסוק, which points to yet another exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the woman was willing, yet she is not forbidden to her husband. The reason is that her marriage is weak. She can always leave through מיאון, even after having children, so she does not become forbidden the way a fully married woman does.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'mistaken' marriage that is not fully binding
She refuses (does מיאון) and leaves the marriage

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said in the name of Rabbi Yishmael:
"And she was not taken" — she is forbidden.
This implies that if she was taken, she is permitted.
And there is another case,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נִתְפָּשָׂה, מוּתֶּרֶת.
phrases.english: where even though she was not taken, she is permitted.
And which case is it? One whose marriage was a mistaken marriage,
phrases.notes: Since the next line says she can do מיאון, this is a girl married off as a minor, whose marriage is not fully binding.

phrases.english: since even with her son riding on her shoulders,
she can refuse and go off on her way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third reading of the same פסוק, which finds a different exception.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman whose marriage can be ended by מיאון is not forbidden to her husband, even if she was willing.

steps.title: Women kidnapped by thieves stay permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that women taken by kidnappers are permitted to their husbands, because whatever happened with the captors counts as אונס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: women who were kidnapped by thieves are permitted to their husbands.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives a practical ruling about kidnapped women. The next lines will challenge it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since they are captives, anything that happened is treated as forced, so they stay permitted. This sets up the challenge from the רבנן: the women's behavior seems to show that they are cooperating willingly.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
Those women who were stolen by thieves
are permitted to their husbands.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה הָנֵי נְשֵׁי דִּגְנַבוּ גַּנָּבֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the idea of אונס to a real case of captive women.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women kidnapped by thieves are permitted to their husbands.

steps.title: But they bring their captors bread
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן challenge רב יהודה: the women bring food to the kidnappers, which looks like willing cooperation.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said to רב יהודה: But they bring them bread!
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן challenge רב יהודה's ruling by pointing to how the women act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the women feed their captors, it seems they are friendly with them and not acting under force. If so, any relationship with them might be willing, and they should be forbidden.

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to Rav Yehuda:
But they bring them bread!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's ruling that kidnapped women are permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Bringing food to the captors suggests the women are cooperating willingly, not forced.

steps.title: They do it out of fear
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that the women bring bread because they are afraid.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is out of fear.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Helping the captors does not show that the women are willing. They are scared of what the kidnappers will do, so the situation is still forced.

phrases.english: Because of fear.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the evidence: the action comes from fear, not willingness.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Feeding the captors shows that the women are willing.
steps.terutzMaskana: It shows fear, so it is still אונס.

steps.title: But they send them arrows
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן push harder: the women even hand the kidnappers arrows, which seems like actively helping them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they send them arrows!
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן give a stronger challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Handing over weapons is a bigger act than bringing food. It looks like the women are on the kidnappers' side.

keyTerms.meaning: Marks an action that is going on now

phrases.english: But they send them arrows!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, stronger challenge after the answer in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the women act only out of fear.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Supplying weapons looks like real loyalty to the captors, not just fear.

steps.title: That is also out of fear
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה gives the same answer: this too is done out of fear.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is out of fear.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers again with the same reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even helping with weapons can come from being afraid of the captors. So it still does not prove that the women are willing.

phrases.english: Because of fear.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the evidence as coming from fear.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Handing over arrows proves the women are willing partners.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is still fear, so they remain permitted.

steps.title: If they go back on their own, they are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה admits a limit: if the kidnappers let the women go and they return to them on their own, they are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But certainly, if the kidnappers let them go and the women go to them on their own, they are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה finishes by stating where his leniency ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fear explains the women's actions only while they are held captive. If they are free and still choose to go back, there is no fear involved, so it counts as רצון.
steps.whatToRemember: Captive women stay permitted, because even helping the captors is explained as fear. Only if they go back by free choice are they forbidden.

phrases.english: Certainly, if they let them go
and they go on their own, they are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the exchange by setting the limit of רב יהודה's ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Kidnapped women are permitted unless, once set free, they return to the captors willingly.

steps.title: Women taken by a king versus women taken by bandits
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that women taken by the government count as captives, but women taken by bandits do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: women captured by the government are treated like captives. Women kidnapped by bandits are not treated like captives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that sorts kidnapped women into two groups: those taken by a king and those taken by bandits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being 'like captives' means we assume the woman was forced and did not go along willingly. The ברייתא gives that status to women taken by a king, but not to women taken by bandits. With bandits, we worry she may have gone along willingly.

keyTerms.meaning: People captured by the government or a king
Like captives, meaning we assume she was forced

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Those captured by the government are like captives.
phrases.notes: 'Like captives' means we assume they were forced and did not agree.

phrases.english: Those stolen by bandits are not like captives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story of רב יהודה and the kidnapped women, the גמרא brings a general ברייתא about types of kidnappers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taken by the government means treated as captives. Taken by bandits means not treated as captives.

steps.title: Another teaching says the reverse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out a ברייתא that rules the exact opposite.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a different ברייתא teaches the reverse!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא it just quoted. Another ברייתא says the opposite: government captives are not like captives, and bandit captives are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two ברייתות directly contradict each other on both cases. The גמרא now has to explain how both can be true.

phrases.english: But it is taught the reverse!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 24 with a ברייתא that says the opposite.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two ברייתות give opposite rulings on the same two cases.

steps.title: Two kinds of kings
steps.stepSummary: The 'king' cases do not clash: one ברייתא means a great king like אחשורוש, the other means a small-time ruler like בן נצר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The clash between the two rulings about a king is not a problem. One is about a king like אחשורוש. The other is about a king like בן נצר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the first half of the contradiction by saying the two ברייתות are talking about different kinds of kings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a powerful king like אחשורוש, the woman knows he will never marry her, so we assume she was forced. With a minor ruler like בן נצר, she might hope he will marry her and go along willingly. So she is not treated as a captive.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
אחשורוש, the example of a truly great king

phrases.english: Government against government is not difficult:
This one is about a kingdom like Achashverosh's,
that one is about a kingdom like ben Netzer's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'king' half of the contradiction in step 25.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to be talking about the same kind of king.
steps.terutzMaskana: A great king like אחשורוש means captive status. A small ruler like בן נצר means no captive status.

steps.title: Two kinds of bandits
steps.stepSummary: The 'bandit' cases do not clash either: one ברייתא means בן נצר, the other means ordinary bandits.
steps.simpleTranslation: The clash between the two rulings about bandits is not a problem. One is about בן נצר. The other is about ordinary bandits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the second half of the contradiction by splitting the bandit cases the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא that says bandit captives are not captives means בן נצר, because she might go along hoping to marry a 'king.' The ברייתא that says they are captives means ordinary bandits. She would never want one of them, so we assume she was forced.

phrases.english: Bandits against bandits is not difficult:
This one is about ben Netzer,
that one is about ordinary bandits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'bandit' half of the contradiction in step 25.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to be talking about the same kind of bandit.
steps.terutzMaskana: בן נצר's men means no captive status. Ordinary bandits means captive status.

steps.title: Is בן נצר a king or a bandit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that בן נצר is called a king in one answer and a bandit in the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: But how can בן נצר be called a king there and a bandit here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions its own answers. בן נצר seems to be called two different things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 26 בן נצר was the example of a 'king.' In step 27 he was the example of a 'bandit.' He cannot be both, so the two answers seem to clash.

phrases.english: And ben Netzer:
there he is called a king,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the answer in step 26 about kings.

phrases.english: and here he is called a bandit!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֶן נֶצַּר הָתָם קָרֵי לֵיהּ מֶלֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the two answers in steps 26 and 27 together.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same person cannot be labeled both a king and a bandit.

steps.title: It depends on whom you compare him to
steps.stepSummary: Yes: next to אחשורוש, בן נצר is a bandit. Next to ordinary bandits, he is a king.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. Compared to אחשורוש, he is a bandit. Compared to ordinary bandits, he is a king.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the double label and explains it. בן נצר's status depends on whom he is being compared to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן נצר sits in the middle. Each ברייתא is comparing him to a different end of the scale. So both answers stand.
steps.whatToRemember: Great king (אחשורוש) means captive status. Ordinary bandits mean captive status. בן נצר, in the middle, means no captive status, because she might hope to marry him.

phrases.english: Yes, compared to Achashverosh, he is a bandit;
compared to ordinary bandits, he is a king.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relative label: it depends on the comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A person must be either a king or a bandit.
steps.terutzMaskana: בן נצר is a bandit compared to a great king, and a king compared to ordinary bandits.

steps.title: A widow married to a כהן גדול must be redeemed
steps.stepSummary: Returning to the משנה's clause about a כהן's wife, אביי rules that a כהן גדול must redeem even a widow he married against the law.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And for a כהן's wife: I will return you to your home province.' אביי said: a widow married to a כהן גדול must be redeemed by him. This is because that clause, 'I will return you to your home province,' applies to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. It quotes the clause about a כהן's wife, and then אביי gives a ruling based on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A widow is forbidden to a כהן גדול, so one might think he owes her nothing. אביי says the clause 'I will return you to your province' still applies, so he must redeem her. He cannot take her back as his wife, but he can send her home.

keyTerms.meaning: I will return you to your home province
A widow married to a כהן גדול, which is forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: The marriage itself is forbidden, but that does not cancel his duty to redeem her. He still has to fulfill the 'return you to your province' clause.

phrases.english: 'And for a priest's wife: I will return you to your province,' etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. A כהן can't take back a captive wife, so he promises to send her home instead.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
A widow married to a High Priest:
he is obligated to redeem her,
because I apply to her the clause:
'And for a priest's wife: I will return you to your province,'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of kinds of kidnappers and returns to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן גדול must redeem a widow he married, because the 'return you to your province' clause applies to her.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the duty to redeem comes from the כתובה terms. A forbidden marriage does not cancel it, as long as the husband can still carry out the clause.
